topics.title: Investigate Intercultural Products, Practices and Perspectives

subtopics.title: Investigate Intercultural Products, Practices and Perspectives (1 of 2)

outcomes.text: NL: Recognize a few typical products and practices related to familiar, everyday life in native and other cultures.
NM: Identify typical cultural products and practices related to familiar, everyday life in native and other cultures to help understand perspectives.
NH: Identify and compare typical products and practices related to familiar, everyday life in native and other cultures to help understand perspectives.
IL: Compare products and practices related to everyday life or personal interests to help understand perspectives in native and other cultures.

subtopics.title: Investigate Intercultural Products, Practices and Perspectives (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: IM: Compare products and practices from concrete researched topics or personal studies to understand perspectives in native and other cultures.
IH: Relate products and practices from concrete researched topics or personal studies to perspectives in native and other cultures.
AL: Analyze how products and practices of public and personal interest are related to perspectives in native and other cultures.
AM: Analyze how global products and practices are related to perspectives in native and other cultures.

topics.title: Compare Intercultural Behaviors

subtopics.title: Compare Intercultural Behaviors (1 of 2)

outcomes.text: NL: Recognize a few very simple behaviors in other cultures.
NM: Identify familiar or everyday behaviors in other cultures.
NH: Identify and compare familiar or everyday behaviors in native and other cultures.
IL: Identify appropriate and inappropriate everyday behaviors in native and other cultures.

subtopics.title: Compare Intercultural Behaviors (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: IM: Compare appropriate and inappropriate behaviors in native and other cultures.
IH: Relate significant differences in behavior to cultural norms in native and other cultures.
AL: Analyze how to adjust behavior according to cultural norms in familiar situations in native and other cultures.
AM: Analyze how to adjust behavior according to cultural norms in familiar and some unfamiliar situations in native and other cultures.

topics.title: Comprehend Authentic Texts* that are Spoken, Written or Signed

subtopics.title: Comprehend Authentic Texts* that are Spoken, Written or Signed (1 of 2)

outcomes.text: NL: Understand a few familiar words or phrases in: Authentic informational texts; Authentic fictional texts; Overheard or observed conversations.
NM: Understand very basic information in: Authentic informational texts; Authentic fictional texts; Overheard or observed conversations.
NH: Understand the topic and some isolated facts in: Authentic informational texts; Authentic fictional texts; Overheard or observed conversations.
IL: Understand the topic and relevant information in: Complex authentic informational texts; complex authentic fictional texts; Complex overheard or observed conversations.

subtopics.title: Comprehend Authentic Texts* that are Spoken, Written or Signed (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: IM: Understand the main idea and supporting information in: Complex authentic informational texts; Complex authentic fictional texts; Complex overheard or observed conversations.
IH: Relate components of: Complex authentic informational texts; Complex authentic fictional texts; Complex overheard or observed conversations.
Analyze components of: Complex authentic informational texts; Complex authentic fictional texts; Complex overheard or observed conversations
Analyze the diversity of components of: Complex authentic informational texts; Complex authentic fictional texts; Complex overheard or observed conversations.

topics.title: Infer Meaning and Nuances of Texts

subtopics.title: Infer Meaning and Nuances of Texts (1 of 2)

outcomes.text: NL: Recognize cognates and familiar or practiced words, as well as nonalphabetic characters, accents, or tone marks.
NM: Recognize cognates and words from context, as well as non-alphabetic characters, accents, or tone marks.
NH: Recognize cognates and infer meaning of unfamiliar words or phrases using context clues and background knowledge.
IL: I Infer meaning of unfamiliar phrases using context clues, background knowledge and related word families.

subtopics.title: Infer Meaning and Nuances of Texts (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: IM: Infer meaning of unfamiliar phrases using context clues, background knowledge and related word families.
IH: Infer underlying message of text via literary devices used, such as anecdotes, satire or suspense.
AL: Infer nuances of text via literary devices used, such as alliteration, juxtaposition or symbolism.
AM: Infer nuances of complex texts via a variety of literary devices used.

topics.title: Recognize and Use Organizational Features of Texts

subtopics.title: Recognize and Use Organizational Features of Texts (1 of 2)

outcomes.text: NL: Recognize visual, aural and organizational features to identify the purpose of very simple texts, such as lists, labels, headlines or titles.
NM: Recognize visual, aural and organizational features to identify the purpose of simple texts, such as infographics, song refrains, simple poems or schedules.
NH: Use visual, aural and organizational features to identify the purpose of simple texts, such as fables, graphics, announcements or instructions.
IL: Use visual, aural and organizational features to identify the author’s purpose and point of view in straightforward texts, such as poetry, short stories, charts, or pros and cons infographics.

subtopics.title: Recognize and Use Organizational Features of Texts (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: IM: Use visual, aural and organizational features to compare the points of view of various authors on similar topics in straightforward texts, such as short novels, survey results, recommendations or cause and effect articles.

IH: Use visual, aural and organizational features to compare and relate the points of view of various authors on similar topics in complex texts, such as novels, descriptions, song lyrics, or problem and solution data reports.
AL: Use visual, aural and organizational features to analyze the points of view of various authors in complex texts, such as novels, reports, rationales or editorials.
AM: Use visual, aural and organizational features to evaluate the points of view or information in a variety of complex texts.

topics.title: Apply Self Questioning Skills

subtopics.title: Apply Self Questioning Skills (1 of 2)

outcomes.text: NL: Use literal or factual self questioning before, during and after engaging with texts, such as “Who, where, when, what or how many?”
NM: Use literal or factual self questioning before, during and after engaging with texts, such as “What time, who is, why or how?”
NH: Use a mixture of literal and inferential self questioning before, during and after engaging with texts, such as “What happened or what might happen next?”
IL: Use inferential selfquestioning before, during and after engaging with texts, such as “Why did the character do this or what can I conclude about the actions of a character?”

subtopics.title: Apply Self Questioning Skills (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: IM: Use analytical selfquestioning before, during and after engaging with texts, such as “What evidence is provided or what is confusing?”
IH: Use evaluative selfquestioning before, during and after engaging with texts, such as “What would I change or do I agree with the author?”
AL: Use critical selfquestioning before, during and after engaging with texts, such as “Who is affected by this or how is this similar to a certain group of people?”
AM: Use critical selfquestioning before, during and after engaging with a variety of complex texts.

topics.title: Make Text Connections

subtopics.title: Make Text Connections (1 of 2)

outcomes.text: NL: Make personal connections to a text using prior knowledge or experiences.
NM: Make personal connections to a text using prior knowledge or experiences.
NH: Make simple text-to-text connections using information from previous texts.
IL: Make text-to-text connections using information from previous texts.

subtopics.title: Make Text Connections (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: IM: Make text-to-world connections using information from previous texts, research and diverse sources.
IH: Make in-depth connections among various texts using researched information from diverse sources.
AL: Make in-depth connections among various texts using researched information from diverse sources.
AM: Integrate information from a variety of complex texts and sources.

topics.title: Select, Use and Cite Resources

subtopics.title: Select, Use and Cite Resources (1 of 2)

outcomes.text: NL: Use digital and cultural resources appropriately.
NM: Use digital and cultural resources appropriately.
NH: Select relevant digital and cultural resources and use them appropriately
IL: Select relevant digital and cultural resources, use appropriately and cite accurately.

subtopics.title: Select, Use and Cite Resources (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: IM: Select relevant digital and cultural resources, use appropriately and cite accurately
IH: Select a variety of relevant digital and cultural resources, use appropriately and cite accurately.
AL: Select a variety of relevant digital and cultural resources, use appropriately and cite accurately.
AM: Select a variety of relevant digital and cultural resources, use appropriately and cite accurately

topics.title: Investigate Intercultural Products, Practices and Perspectives

subtopics.title: Investigate Intercultural Products, Practices and Perspectives (1 of 2)

outcomes.text: NL: Identify a few very familiar products and practices in native and other cultures, such as: Holidays, celebrations; School supplies, school schedules.

NM: Identify similarities and differences between typical products and practices to help understand perspectives in native and other cultures, such as: Food, mealtimes, importance of dining together; Clothing, leisure activities, appropriate dress.

NH: Identify and make simple comparisons between typical products and practices to help understand perspectives in native and other cultures, such as: Video and cell phone school life, importance of extracurricular activities; Currency, shopping, saving vs spending.

IL Compare and contrast everyday products, practices and perspectives in native and other cultures, such as: Professions, work hours, attitudes toward vacation time; TV channels, prime time programming, popularity of various shows.

subtopics.title: Investigate Intercultural Products, Practices and Perspectives (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: IM: Compare and contrast the relationships among everyday products, practices and perspectives in native and other cultures, such as: Arts, dancing, ideas of beauty; Literature, cultural events, importance of traditions.

IH: Compare and contrast the relationships among familiar and unfamiliar products, practices and perspectives in native and other cultures, such as: Green products, recycling, earth friendly beliefs; Historical events, social norms, value of demonstrations.

AL: Analyze the relationships among products, practices and perspectives of public and personal interest in native and other cultures, such as: Pharmaceuticals, use of antibiotics, attitudes toward vaccinations; National identity, globalized practices, perspectives on use of foreign words.

AM: Analyze the relationships among global products, practices and perspectives in native and other cultures, such as: Housing, gentrification, accessibility of social services; Minimum wage, unemployment, accessibility of leave of absence.

topics.title: Comprehend Informational Media or Content

subtopics.title: Comprehend Informational Media or Content (1 of 2)

outcomes.text: NL: Recognize a few individual words in a recorded media or public announcement.
NM: Recognize repeated words, taglines or short quotes from sources such as commercials, travel ads or movie trailers.
NH: Identify individual facts from radio or video ads, such as product name, cost and where to buy it.
IL: Identify the general topic and basic facts or information from a cultural product such as a documentary or vlog.

subtopics.title: Comprehend Informational Media or Content (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: IM: Determine the targeted age group and demographics from publicity for newly released or recorded media, such as social media feed, film, or commercials.
IH: Determine and break down the elements of two products, such as marketing strategies in video ads or bias in election coverage.
AL: Analyze the elements of a modern-day product, service, or global issue and compare them to prior strategies used to promote or inform about it.
AM: Analyze the effects of different types of marketing on demographic groups.

topics.title: Comprehend Fictional Media or Content

subtopics.title: Comprehend Fictional Media or Content (1 of 2)

outcomes.text: NL: Recognize common opening and closing words in oral or video storytelling
NM: Identify simple phrases describing physical or personality traits, such as of a cartoon or movie character.
NH: Identify individual story elements in an episode of a video series, such as characters, setting or theme.
IL: Compare events in a fictional video series, such as connections, sequencing or importance to the story line.

subtopics.title: Comprehend Fictional Media or Content (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: IM: Compare two short literary or fictional films, such as characters or genre.
IH: Analyze a fictional film to determine abstract story elements, such as the moral of the story or relationships among characters.
AL: Connect elements such as causes, outcomes or impact of an event in a fictional film to a similar historical or current event.
AM: Analyze the differences in a fictional film from the facts of the historical event upon which it is based.

topics.title: Follow Instructions

subtopics.title: Follow Instructions (1 of 2)

outcomes.text: NL: Follow simple directions for classroom tasks or routines.
NM: Follow two step directions, such as to pack a suitcase or fill in a graphic organizer.
NH: Follow simple steps in an online video, such as to make food or draw an image.
IL: Follow multi step instructions, such as to create a craft or take medication.

subtopics.title: Follow Instructions (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: IM: Follow a series of directions, such as to a destination or to build a model from a kit.
IH: Follow an online video tutorial, such as to change a tire or redecorate a bedroom.
AL: Follow how-to videos for gamers or job interviews.
AM: Follow procedural changes introduced at the beginning of a board or council meeting

topics.title: Comprehend Overheard or Observed Conversations

subtopics.title: Comprehend Overheard or Observed Conversations (1 of 2)

outcomes.text: NL: Recognize very basic information or questions from overheard or observed conversations, such as greetings, introductions, name, title or age.
NM: Recognize basic information and questions from overheard or observed conversations, such as phone number, residence, family members and occupation.
NH: Identify simple information and questions from a conversation among peers about topics such as weekend plans or preferences.
IL: Identify details from a planning session, such as what people should wear to a dance or a server’s questions about someone’s food order.

subtopics.title: Comprehend Overheard or Observed Conversations (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: IM: Identify storyline and details from a conversation, such as events from a bad date or questions between team members about a collaborative project.
IH: Determine the cause of an argument or dialog, such as a conversation between people in a public place or an interview of a celebrity.
AL: Determine points of view from a discussion about such topics as room remodeling between designer and customer or debates on candidates’ platform and record.
AM: Analyze the results of a celebrity’s personal and professional choices during their rise to fame.

topics.title: Investigate Intercultural Products, Practices and Perspectives

subtopics.title: Investigate Intercultural Products, Practices and Perspectives (1 of 2)

outcomes.text: NL: identify a few very familiar products and practices in native and other cultures, such as: Greetings, how people greet others; Clothing, how people dress.

NM: identify similarities and differences between typical products and practices to understand perspectives in native and other cultures, such as: Decorations, how people celebrate, reasons for celebrations; Types of houses, dining habits, size of rooms.

NH: Identify and make simple comparisons between typical products and practices to help understand perspectives in native and other cultures, such as: Meals, grocery shopping , food trends; Rooms in a house, use of space, size of appliances.

IL: Compare and contrast everyday products, practices and perspectives in native and other cultures, such as: Graphic novels, reading, the role of literacy in learning and life; Landmarks, behavior at landmarks, how landmarks represent national identity.

subtopics.title: Investigate Intercultural Products, Practices and Perspectives (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: IM: Compare and contrast the relationships among everyday products, practices and perspectives in native and other cultures, such as: Invitations, special occasions, cultural value of celebrations; Ancient architecture, religious ceremonies, impact of mythology.

IH: Compare and contrast the relationships among familiar and unfamiliar products, practices and perspectives in native and other cultures, such as: Family structures, weddings, treatment of elders; Obituaries, funerals, attitudes toward death.

AL: Analyze the relationships among products, practices and perspectives in native and other cultures, such as: Love poems, marriage, discrimination; Political groups, public speaking, social class nuances.

AM: Analyze the relationships among global products, practices and perspectives in native and other cultures, such as: Educational testing, ceremonies, value of entrance exams; Stereotypes, immigration policies, attitudes toward ethnic diversity.

topics.title: Comprehend Informational Media or Content

subtopics.title: Comprehend Informational Media or Content (1 of 2)

outcomes.text: NL: Recognize a few individual words in texts, such as school schedules, menus or headlines.
NM: Recognize items in texts such as a shopping list, food label categories or information from a weather forecast with symbols.
NH: Recognize the topic and a few details in texts, such as a family tree or historical account.
IL: Identify the position and key components in more complex texts, such as a job posting or product review.

subtopics.title: Comprehend Informational Media or Content (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: IM: Understand the differences and nuances from full texts, such as job descriptions and product reviews in order to choose the best option.
IH: Determine and break down information from complex texts, such as articles or organizational websites.
AL: Connect the effects of influential articles on organized or spontaneous events.
AM: Analyze the impact of sequential historical events on modern-day happenings.

topics.title: Comprehend Fictional Media or Content

subtopics.title: Comprehend Fictional Media or Content (1 of 2)

outcomes.text: NL: Recognize characters’ names or a few words in texts, such as a fairy tale or movie poster.
NM: Recognize simple facts or phrases from captions in texts, such as an illustrated book or a character description.
NH: Identify individual story elements from texts such as a scene in a play, including characters, setting or theme.
IL: Compare events in two fictional short stories or poems, such as theme, connections, sequencing or importance to the story line.

subtopics.title: Comprehend Fictional Media or Content (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: IM: Compare short literary works from different genres, determining key components such as plot points, points of view, or conflicts.
IH: Determine and break down the tone, moral, and sequence of events in texts such as a folktale, play, or poem.
AL: Compare fictional texts to determine culturally ingrained messages and perspectives such as folktales, plays, or poems.
AM: Analyze the effects of literary movements on societal cultural shifts and vice versa.

topics.title: Follow Instructions

subtopics.title: Follow Instructions (1 of 2)

outcomes.text: NL: Follow familiar instructions for routines, such as posted directions in the classroom.
NM: Follow simple familiar guides, such as a printed schedule or simple website recipe.
NH: Follow simple directions, such as to set up a new phone or complete a scavenger hunt.
IL: Follow multi-step directions, such as how to create an outfit for a cultural event.

subtopics.title: Follow Instructions (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: IM: Follow complex multistep instructions to complete a task, such as getting to a destination.
IH: Follow multi-step instructions to complete a task, such as to submit an online job application.
AL: Follow a multi-step guide to complete a task such as writing an argumentative essay.
AM: Follow complex instructions, such as the logistics for renting a place through a homesharing website.

topics.title: Comprehend Overheard or Observed Conversations

subtopics.title: Comprehend Overheard or Observed Conversations (1 of 2)

outcomes.text: NL: Recognize question words in texts such as a text message or email.
NM: Recognize common abbreviations in texts such as a social media thread
NH: Identify basic facts such as in a group text or social media thread.
IL: Understand the main idea or opinions expressed in written texts, such as a social media thread.

subtopics.title: Comprehend Overheard or Observed Conversations (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: IM: Compare opinions and perspectives, such as of individuals participating in an online discussion or social media thread.
IH: Determine the main points of a debate between people in a blog post or article comments.
AL: Compare cultural perspectives that influence the opinions of participants in an online thread, such as the definition of family.
AM: Analyze the role of emotions in social media threads or online editorials.

topics.title: Investigate Intercultural Products, Practices and Perspectives

subtopics.title: Investigate Intercultural Products, Practices and Perspectives (1 of 2)

outcomes.text: NL: Identify a few typical products and practices related to familiar, everyday life in native and other cultures.
NM: Identify typical products and practices related to familiar, everyday life to help understand perspectives of native and other cultures.
NH: Identify products and practices related to everyday life to help understand perspectives of native and other cultures.
IL: Compare products and practices related to everyday life and personal interests or studies to help understand perspectives of native and other cultures.

subtopics.title: Investigate Intercultural Products, Practices and Perspectives (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: IM: Compare products and practices of personal interest or researched topics to help understand perspectives of native and other cultures.
IH: Compare products and practices of personal interest or researched topics to help understand perspectives of native and other cultures.
AL: Share how products and practices of public and personal interest are related to perspectives of native and other cultures.
AM: Share how global products and practices are related to perspectives of native and other cultures.

topics.title: Interact with Culturally Appropriate Language and Behaviors

subtopics.title: Interact with Culturally Appropriate Language and Behaviors (1 of 2)

outcomes.text: NL: Interact in very familiar intercultural situations using practiced language and behaviors and show cultural awareness by recognizing a few culturally inappropriate behaviors.
NM: Interact in very familiar intercultural situations using practiced language and behaviors and show cultural awareness by recognizing culturally inappropriate behaviors.
NH: Interact in familiar, everyday intercultural situations using practiced language and behaviors and show cultural awareness by recognizing culturally inappropriate behaviors.
IL: Converse in familiar situations at school, work or play using appropriate learned behaviors and avoiding major social blunders.

subtopics.title: Interact with Culturally Appropriate Language and Behaviors (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: IM: Converse in familiar situations at school, work or play using appropriate learned behaviors and avoiding major social blunders.
IH: Converse in familiar situations at school, work or play using appropriate learned behaviors and avoiding major social blunders, recognizing that significant differences exist among cultures.
AL: Converse in familiar and some unfamiliar situations showing some awareness of subtle cultural differences by adjusting behavior accordingly.
AM: Converse comfortably in familiar and some unfamiliar situations showing some awareness of subtle cultural differences by adjusting behavior accordingly.

topics.title: Exchange Information and Ideas

subtopics.title: Exchange Information and Ideas (1 of 2)

outcomes.text: NL: Provide basic information on very familiar topics.
NM: Request and share simple information on familiar or everyday topics.
NH: Request and share information on familiar and everyday topics.
IL: Converse on a variety of familiar topics.

subtopics.title: Exchange Information and Ideas (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: IM: Converse on a variety of familiar topics and some concrete researched topics.
IH: Converse on a variety of familiar and concrete researched topics.
AL: Discuss a variety of familiar and some unfamiliar concrete researched topics.
AM: Maintain discussions on a variety of familiar and unfamiliar concrete topics and some academic, social or professional topics.

topics.title: Meet Personal Needs or Address Situations

subtopics.title: Meet Personal Needs or Address Situations (1 of 2)

outcomes.text: NL: Express a few basic personal needs in very familiar situations.
NM: Express basic needs in familiar or everyday situations.
NH: Interact with others to meet basic needs in familiar and everyday situations.
IL: Interact with others to meet needs in familiar and everyday situations.

subtopics.title: Meet Personal Needs or Address Situations (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: IM: Interact with others to meet needs in a variety of familiar and everyday situations.
IH: Meet needs in a variety of familiar and everyday situations, sometimes involving a complication.
AL: Resolve an unexpected complication in a familiar or everyday situation.
AM: Resolve an unexpected complication in some unfamiliar situations.

topics.title: Express, React to and Support Preferences, Opinions or Viewpoints

subtopics.title: Express, React to and Support Preferences, Opinions or Viewpoints (1 of 2)

outcomes.text: NL: Express a few basic preferences or feelings.
NM: Express basic preferences or feelings and react to those of others.
NH: Express, ask about and react to simple preferences, feelings or opinions on familiar topics.
IL: Express, ask about and react with some detail to preferences, feelings or opinions on familiar topics.

subtopics.title: Express, React to and Support Preferences, Opinions or Viewpoints (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: IM: Exchange and react to preferences, feelings, opinions and simple advice on a variety of familiar topics.
IH: Explain and react to viewpoints, emotions and advice on a variety of familiar topics and some concrete researched topics.
AL: Explain, react to and compare viewpoints, emotions and advice on a variety of familiar and unfamiliar concrete researched topics.
AM: Support, react to, and compare viewpoints and emotions and on a variety of familiar and unfamiliar concrete researched topics.

topics.title: Communicate, React and Show Interest

subtopics.title: Communicate, React and Show Interest (1 of 2)

outcomes.text: NL: Use familiar, relevant vocabulary and structures and rehearsed or imitated cultural behaviors to communicate, react and show interest.
NM: Use familiar, relevant vocabulary and structures and rehearsed or imitated cultural behaviors to communicate, react and show interest.
NH: Use culturally appropriate and relevant language and rehearsed or learned behaviors to communicate, react and show interest.
IL: Use culturally appropriate and relevant language, syntax and learned behaviors to communicate, react and show interest.

subtopics.title: Communicate, React and Show Interest (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: IM: Use culturally appropriate and relevant language, syntax and learned behaviors to communicate, react and show interest.
IH: Use culturally appropriate and relevant content and syntax and begin to adjust language or behaviors as needed to communicate, react and show interest.
AL: Use culturally appropriate and relevant content and syntax and adjust language or behaviors as needed to communicate, react and show interest.
AM: Use culturally appropriate and relevant content and syntax and adjust language or behaviors as needed to communicate, react and show interest.

topics.title: Continue and Extend Conversations

subtopics.title: Continue and Extend Conversations (1 of 2)

outcomes.text: NL: Use a few very simple verbal or nonverbal interjections, rejoinders or requests for clarification.
NM: Use very simple verbal and nonverbal interjections, rejoinders, requests for clarification, interrogatives or transition words.
NH: Use simple interjections, rejoinders, requests for clarification, interrogatives and transition words.
IL: Use a variety of simple interjections, rejoinders, interrogatives and transitions.

subtopics.title: Continue and Extend Conversations (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: IM: Use some complex interjections, rejoinders, interrogatives and transitions.
IH: Use a variety of complex interjections, rejoinders, interrogatives and transitions.
AL: Use a variety of complex interjections, rejoinders, interrogatives and transitions.
AM: Use a variety of complex interjections, rejoinders, interrogatives and transitions.

topics.title: Increase Comprehensibility and Clarity of Expression

outcomes.text: NL: Increase comprehensibility using gestures, hand shapes, facial expressions, repetition or awareness of pronunciation.
NM: Increase comprehensibility using gestures, hand shapes, facial expressions, repetition, word substitution or awareness of pronunciation, tone or pitch.
NH: Increase comprehensibility and clarify information using word substitution, rephrasing, circumlocution and attention to pronunciation, tone or pitch.
IL: Enhance comprehensibility and clarify information using simple explanations, rephrasing, circumlocution and some consistency in pronunciation, tone or pitch.

AL: Enhance comprehensibility and clarity using paraphrasing, elaboration, consistent pronunciation, tone or pitch, register, and rate of speech.
AM: Enhance comprehensibility and clarity using paraphrasing, elaboration, consistent pronunciation, tone or pitch, register, and rate of speech.

NM: Infer meaning of unfamiliar language from gestures, facial and body expressions or context clues during simple interactions.
NH: Infer meaning of unfamiliar language from gestures, facial and body expressions, context clues or topic of conversation.
IL: Infer meaning of unfamiliar language from context or topic of conversation

subtopics.title: Infer Meaning of Unfamiliar Language (2 of 2)

units.title: INTERPERSONAL LISTENING AND SPEAKING OR SIGNING

topics.title: Investigate Intercultural Products, Practices and Perspectives

subtopics.title: Investigate Intercultural Products, Practices and Perspectives (1 of 2)

outcomes.text: NL: Answer a few simple questions about very familiar cultural products and practices in native and other cultures, such as: Flags, flag design; Days of the week, telling the date.

NM: Ask and answer a few simple questions about typical cultural products and practices to help understand perspectives in native and other cultures, such as: Invitations, special occasions, reasons for celebrations; Rooms in a house, house design, what makes a house a home.

NH: Exchange simple information about similarities and differences between typical cultural products and practices to help understand perspectives in native and other cultures, such as: School schedules, course selection, importance of academics; National parks, study of geography, importance of natural resources.

IL: Exchange information to make simple comparisons between everyday cultural products and practices to help understand perspectives in native and other cultures, such as: Monuments, traditional events, national identity; Daily routines, leisure activities, value of free time.

subtopics.title: Investigate Intercultural Products, Practices and Perspectives (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: IM: Exchange information to compare everyday cultural products, practices and perspectives in native and other cultures, such as: Fashion houses, clothing trends, attitude toward thrift shops; Social media, ways people communicate, technology’s effects on socializing.

IH: Exchange information to compare the relationships among familiar and some unfamiliar cultural products, practices and perspectives in native and other cultures, such as: Commercials, advertising, what sells a product; Buildings, neighborhoods, how city design affects lifestyles

AL: Exchange information to compare the relationships among a variety of unfamiliar cultural products, practices and perspectives in native and other cultures, such as: Migrant workers, seasonal hiring, acculturation; Public schools, educational testing, role of education in quality of life.

AM: Exchange information to compare the relationships among global cultural products, practices and perspectives in native and other cultures, such as: Professional or social schedules, influence of time on scheduling, cultural concepts of time. Environmental problems, solutions to such problems, respect for such solutions.

topics.title: Interact with Culturally Appropriate Language and Behaviors

subtopics.title: Interact with Culturally Appropriate Language and Behaviors (1 of 2)

outcomes.text: NL: Imitate culturally appropriate behavior at a festival or holiday celebration.
NM: Use rehearsed culturally appropriate behavior when purchasing an item.
NH: Use foreign currency with an understanding of its conversion value.
IL: Demonstrate culturally appropriate greeting and leave-taking behaviors when visiting a business.

subtopics.title: Interact with Culturally Appropriate Language and Behaviors (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: IM: Demonstrate respect through culturally appropriate dress and voice volume when visiting historical sites.
IH: Demonstrate culturally appropriate reactions and behaviors when trying unfamiliar food or drink.
AL: Offer culturally appropriate gifts in a socially conventional manner as a guest at a celebration.
